newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Overnight guilders ease on new liquidity pact.
newsitem.headline: Overnight guilders ease on new liquidity pact.

text.p: Dutch call money eased a touch on Friday in the wake of a new short-term liquidity allocation ahead of the long weekend.
Overnight guilders were quoting at 3.06 percent bid, compared with 3.12 percent on Thursday, while other rates held steady in a relatively quiet session.
"Today's allocation appears to have given players the liquidity they need to see them through the Whitsun weekend," a dealer said.
The Dutch central bank earlier allotted 3.49 billion guilders under a seven-day pact priced at 2.9 percent.
It said individual banks had been awarded 14.1 percent of the amounts applied for up to 4.0 billion guilders.

Dealers reported some trade in the finance ministry's June and July short-term Dutch Treasury Certificate (DTC) borrowing instruments, which they said were reasonably priced at 3.15 and 3.16 percent respectively.
The guilder was quoted at 112.46 per 100 marks, down a touch from Thursday's 112.445 fixing.
